2607.26574.title: Recover, Decode, Reguard: Guard-Agnostic Defense Amplification againstEncoded VLM Jailbreaks
2607.26574.paper_summary: Safety classifiers ("guards") are the dominant black-box defense for vision-language models, yet they judge an input's surface form, not its meaning: a harmful request re-encoded as set theory, formal logic, a rare language, code, or an image of text slips past a guard that would block it in plain language -- the decode gap. The natural fix is a guard-agnostic recover-and-decode amplifier that transcribes image content and restates encoded text into its plain payload before the guard, so any off-the-shelf classifier can screen the true request. We build this amplifier and evaluate it against the attacker's best case: an ensemble of eleven attacks, scoring a behavior as broken if any succeeds (best-of-suite, following AutoAttack) -- rarely reported for jailbreak defenses, yet ~3.5x the per-attack mean. This exposes our central finding: an empirical safety-utility ceiling for the non-iterative recovery defenses we evaluate, across five guards and two target VLMs. The amplifier only partly closes the gap -- the undefended ensemble breaks 89-91% of behaviors, and the best guard-plus-amplifier still leaves 63-65% -- and its gain over the guard alone is significant in only four of ten guard-target pairs. It is guard-agnostic at the interface, but not uniformly so in effect. A modular reguard layer closes much of the residual, yet drives benign over-refusal to 81-92% for well-calibrated guards; the one laxer guard that stays usable never reaches deployable safety (48% ensemble ASR). No configuration we evaluate reaches both low attack-success and low over-refusal, for the pipeline we study and for representation-shifting attacks -- encodings and cross-modal renders that leave a legible payload, not pixel- or embedding-space attacks. We contribute the amplifier, an ensemble evaluation that makes the trade-off visible, and a map of where recovery-based VLM defense works and where it does not.
2607.26574.paper_summary_zh: 安全分類器（“守衛”）是視覺-語言模型的主要黑盒防禦，但它們評估的是輸入的表面形式，而非其意義：一個有害的請求如果以集合論、形式邏輯、一種罕見語言、代碼或文字圖像重新編碼，就能逃過一個會阻擋普通語言的守衛——這就是解碼差距。自然的解決方案是一個與守衛無關的恢復與解碼放大器，它在守衛之前將圖像內容轉錄並將編碼文本重新陳述為其普通有效載荷，這樣任何現成的分類器都可以篩選出真正的請求。我們構建了這個放大器，並對其進行了評估，針對攻擊者的最佳情況：一組由十一種攻擊組成的集合，如果任何一種成功則將行為評分為失效（最佳套件，遵循AutoAttack）——這在越獄防禦中很少報告，但每次攻擊的平均值約為3.5倍。這揭示了我們的核心發現：我們評估的非迭代恢復防禦在五個守衛和兩個目標VLM中存在一個實證的安全-效用上限。放大器僅部分縮小了這一差距——未防禦的集合破壞了89-91%的行為，而最佳的守衛加放大器仍然留下63-65%——並且在十對守衛-目標配對中，只有四對的增益在守衛單獨使用時是顯著的。它在介面上是與守衛無關的，但在效果上並不均勻。一個模塊化的重新守衛層縮小了大部分剩餘，但對於良好校準的守衛，卻將良性過度拒絕推高至81-92%；唯一一個較為寬鬆的守衛仍然可用，但從未達到可部署的安全性（48%的集合ASR）。我們評估的沒有任何配置同時達到低攻擊成功率和低過度拒絕，無論是對於我們研究的管道還是對於表示轉移攻擊——這些編碼和跨模態渲染留下了可讀的有效載荷，而不是像素或嵌入空間的攻擊。我們貢獻了放大器、一個使權衡可見的集合評估，以及一個關於基於恢復的VLM防禦在何處有效、何處無效的地圖。
